tutorial: No FreeCAD wiki tutorial covers measuring a scan (Mesh_to_Part.md, Mesh_FromPartShape.md, Inspection_Workbench.md and Reverse_Engineering_Workbench.md describe the commands, with no worked answer key). As the task asked, the model needs no scan file: the 'scan' is a known solid meshed through the tools — a 60 × 40 × 20 mm block with a Ø12 through bore at (20, 20) and, on the scanned copy only, a 10 × 10 × 1 mm pocket in the top at x 40–50, y 15–25 — so every fit, dimension, deviation and thickness has a worked-out answer. The unworn block is the deviation reference; the pocket is the 'wear'.

thickness.why: the pocket's wall at x 50 to the face at x 60; the bore's wall to the nearest face is 14

expected.simulated: Every number above was also read by running the add-on's own handlers in plain Python on a mesh of the same part built with numpy (boundary-vertex triangulation, then the add-on's densify). FreeCAD's mesher will place vertices differently: counts and areas marked 'about' move by a few per cent, the dimensions do not. The FreeCAD-only steps (meshing, scan_open { object }, the shadow, section_to_sketch, element_to_document, deviation_open_reference { body }, pack_write, manual_check, manual_render) were not run anywhere.

conventions.chunks: Run in order, in chunks of 20; the comments in the patch notes mark seven natural chunks but any cut works — calls name elements, sections and bodies by the names they were given, never by an earlier answer's id (one exception: <BODY>).
conventions.<JOB>: Only when a heavy read (scan_qa, scan_segment, scan_heightmap, section_fit, deviation_align, deviation_measure, deviation_set_target, deviation_hotspots, deviation_volume, deviation_export, thickness_measure, manual_check, manual_render) answers with status running instead of its result: the answer's job field fills <JOB> in job_status { job: "<JOB>", wait: 25 }. Inside a batch heavy reads run inline and no job id comes.
conventions.frame: All coordinates are the CAD frame of the block until the align_ calls of chunk 6; each of those says the box it should leave.
conventions.builderCalls: doc_new, part_primitive, part_boolean, part_transform, meshobj_from_shape, mesh_densify, mesh_use_edited and pd_pad belong to other families (arguments read from their schemas, not hardened here): if one answers differently, any way of getting a body Block, a body Worn and a mesh object labelled WornScan serves.
conventions.<BODY>: section_to_sketch's answer field body (call 58) fills <BODY> in the pd_pad after it (call 59): a new Body takes FreeCAD's next free label (Body002 on the Mac), never a fixed one. The one call here that needs an earlier answer; to avoid it, make the Body first with pd_body_new { name } and give it to section_to_sketch as body.
conventions.refusals: A call whose expect starts REFUSED is meant to be refused: check the code and that the message says what to do next.
conventions.files: Relative paths go in the session's output folder.

notCovered: scan_open { path, units }: needs a file — after wear_rebuild, scan_open { path: "worn-repaired.stl", discard: true } opens one made by the model itself (it replaces the scan and its elements, so it is left out of the run); expect box.size [60, 40, 20] and min deviation about 0 after a new deviation_align
deviation_open_reference { path }: the same file serves; a STEP needs export first

deviation_align modes auto and local: auto took 32 s on this part in plain Python and, on this part, has two equal poses against the unworn block (top and bottom swap) — ambiguous: true is the right answer there; local needs vertices from scan_query { fields: "ids" }

deviation_hotspots { on: "reference" } and deviation_export { side: "reference" }: before the fix the reference-side reading took 1,419 s in plain Python on this part (1.8 million readings, nine times its own cap); with the cap honoured it should take a few minutes — run job_start { tool: "deviation_hotspots", arguments: { on: "reference" }, wait: false } once live to time it on the Mac: expect readings under 200,000, coveredPct 100, withinTolerancePct about 99, mostMissing -1.0 near [45, 20, 20], mostExcess 0

scan_noise's reading, scan_thread's match, a non-zero draft, a rotational pattern count, sheet / rims in scan_qa: a noise-free prismatic block has none of them — they need a real scan (the add-on's plain-Python tests cover them on synthetic noisy meshes)

element_fit kinds sphere, cone, torus, circle, point and knownDiameter; element_construct's other methods; dimension types on spheres and loc-coaxiality: no such feature on the block (covered by tests/test_fits.py, test_measuring_core.py)
fit_scan_export { what: "stl" | "ini" } and a non-zero printer error: the scan is the CAD itself, so every correction is zero
scan_snapshot_latest with a shot, scan_snapshot_wait as a job: only the person's camera key (Alt+Shift+S) makes a shot
manual_plan export / import, pack_setup files and upstream entries, scanner export / import, fit_scan_setup keymap: plain file round trips, covered by the plain-Python tests

The worker-thread hand-over (docstate.on_gui_thread): proven only on stand-ins; live, run deviation_align as a job (job_start { tool: "deviation_align", arguments: { mode: "auto" }, wait: false }) and watch that FreeCAD stays up and the scan object's Placement has followed once job_status says done
